title: Wedding Guests
short: Reply on time, bring only the guests named on the invitation, follow the dress code, give a gift (often from the registry), and let the couple shine.
trouble: Learners bring a date who was not invited, or ask the couple why they were not given a plus-one. Whether guests should avoid all-white outfits is debated; most writers advise leaving white to the bride.

blocks.html: A wedding invitation calls on everything you know about replying, dress codes and gifts. It is a day the couple has planned for a long time, and a good guest helps it go the way they hoped.
Reply on time, bring only the guests named on the invitation, follow the dress code, give a gift (often from the registry), and let the couple shine.

A wedding is planned to the seat: caterers need a count, and every added guest costs money and space. That is why the reply date matters and why only those named are invited. The registry tells guests what the couple would like, which spares everyone guesswork. And the day is about the couple, so a guest's job is to celebrate them, not to draw attention.

cards.text: Replying by the date on the card
Bringing a date when the invitation names only you
cards.why: Only those named are invited; the couple planned for each seat.

cards.text: Choosing a gift from the registry
Asking the couple why you didn't get a plus-one
cards.why: It puts them on the spot about a budget they had to set.

cards.text: Making a long speech no one asked you to give
cards.why: Let the couple and their chosen speakers shine.

blocks.title: One name on the envelope
blocks.q: Leo's wedding invitation is addressed to "Mr. Leo Novak." He has been dating Ruby for a month. May he bring her?
steps: The invitation names exactly who is invited: Leo alone.
He replies for himself only and does not ask the couple to add Ruby.

blocks.title: The gift
blocks.q: Priya can't attend her cousin's wedding. Should she still send a gift?
steps: Many writers say a gift is customary for a wedding you are invited to, whether or not you attend; customs vary.
She sends a gift from the registry, or a card with a warm note, as her budget allows.
blocks.a: A gift or a warm card is a kind way to celebrate from afar.

blocks.title: What to wear
blocks.q: Nora's invitation says "cocktail attire." She has a white dress she loves. What would most writers suggest?
steps: Whether guests should avoid all-white outfits is debated.
Most writers advise leaving white to the bride, so a color is the safe choice.
A cocktail dress in any other color fits the code.
blocks.a: Choose another color; most writers leave white to the bride.

blocks.html: Bringing a date who was not invited, or asking the couple why you were not given a plus-one. Whether guests should avoid all-white outfits is debated; most writers advise leaving white to the bride.

Customs differ: weddings vary widely by culture, faith and family, from what guests wear to how gifts are given, and some couples ask for no gifts at all. Follow the invitation and the couple's wishes.
